claims.claim: GFP-tagged HCP-1CENP-F, HCP-2CENP-F, and CLS-2CLASP are absent from kinetochores upon BUB-1 depletion.
claims.source: We imaged C. elegans zygotes expressing endogenous GFP-tagged HCP-1CENP-F or HCP-2CENP-F, or a GFP-tagged CLS-2CLASP transgene, and confirmed their absence from kinetochores upon BUB-1 depletion (Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: Following depletion of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP, chromosomes do not congress, and chromosomes and spindle poles separate prematurely 40 s after NEBD concomitant with sister chromatid co-segregation.
claims.source: In line with previous observations, following depletion of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP, chromosomes did not congress, and chromosomes and spindle poles separated prematurely 40 s after NEBD concomitant with sister chromatid co-segregation towards the same spindle pole (Figure 1B–H; Video 1) (Cheeseman et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 1B-H and Video 1.

claims.claim: Early pole and chromosome separation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP is not caused by premature anaphase onset.
claims.source: This early pole and chromosome separation was not caused by premature anaphase onset, as the fluorescent signal of a Separase activation sensor remained on chromosomes well after they completed separation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E) (Kim et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-E.

claims.claim: A vast majority of chromosomes remain mono-oriented in HCP-1/2CENP-F- or CLS-2CLASP-depleted zygotes.
claims.source: Instead, a vast majority of chromosomes remained mono-oriented in HCP-1/2CENP-F- or CLS-2CLASP-depleted zygotes (Figure 1F–H) (Cheeseman et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 1F-H.

claims.claim: Sister chromatid co-segregation in HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP depletion is due to improperly mono-oriented chromosomes rather than premature mitotic exit.
claims.source: This indicates that the sister chromatid co-segregation phenotype resulting from depletion of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP is due to improperly mono-oriented chromosomes rather than premature mitotic exit.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 depletion restores biorientation and rescues the sister chromatid segregation failure typical of CLS-2CLASP depletion.
claims.source: Strikingly BUB-1 depletion restored biorientation and rescued the sister chromatid segregation failure typical of CLS-2CLASP depletion (Figure 1B,C; Video 1).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1B,C and Video 1.

claims.claim: BUB-1 depletion rescues sister chromatid segregation in Δhcp-2 mutants co-depleted of HCP-1CENP-F.
claims.source: We also observed similar sister chromatid segregation rescue by co-depleting BUB-1 and HCP-1CENP-F or HCP-2CENP-F, in CRIPSR-cas9 generated hcp-2 (Δhcp-2) (Figure 1B,C; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C) and hcp-1 (Δhcp-1; Figure 1—figure supplement 2D–E) deletion mutants respectively.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: BUB-1 and HCP-1CENP-F (or HCP-2CENP-F) co-depleted embryos display delayed congression and merotelic attachments.
claims.source: BUB-1 and HCP-1CENP-F (or HCP-2CENP-F) co-depleted embryos displayed a 'BUB-1-like' phenotype with delayed congression (Figure 1B,C) and merotelic attachments to both spindle poles evidenced by bent kinetochores during metaphase and kinetochore stretches during anaphase (Figure 1F–H).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 1B,C and Figure 1F-H.

claims.claim: BUB-1 prevents chromosome biorientation, and this activity is revealed in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that BUB-1 prevents chromosome biorientation, and that this activity is revealed in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 recruitment to kinetochores depends on phosphorylated MELT repeats located in the N-terminal part of KNL-1.
claims.source: BUB-1 recruitment to kinetochores depends on phosphorylated MELT repeats located in the N-terminal part of the kinetochore scaffolding protein KNL-1 (Vleugel et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: KNL-1Δ85-505 lacks all MELT repeats and abolishes BUB-1 recruitment to kinetochores.
claims.source: To abolish BUB-1 recruitment to kinetochores, we used a C. elegans strain expressing a truncation mutant of KNL-1 (KNL-1Δ85-505), which lacks all MELT repeats (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) (Moyle et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: In the presence of KNL-1Δ85-505, co-depleted zygotes display delayed congression and bioriented merotelic attachments.
claims.source: In contrast, in the presence of KNL-1Δ85-505, and therefore in the absence of BUB-1 at kinetochores (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), co-depleted zygotes displayed a 'BUB-1-like' phenotype with delayed congression and bioriented merotelic attachments (Figure 2B–D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Video 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 2B-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: BUB-1 inhibitory activity on biorientation depends on its kinetochore localisation.
claims.source: Together, these results show that BUB-1 inhibitory activity on biorientation depends on its kinetochore localisation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N, but not BUB-1D814N, lead to delayed anaphase onset.
claims.source: In line with previous findings on BUB-1 function in the regulation of anaphase onset, BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R ;D847N, but not BUB-1D814N, led to delayed anaphase onset (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B) (Kim et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: All BUB-1 mutants (BUB-1ΔKD, BUB-1K718R;D847N, BUB-1D814N) localize to kinetochores in absence of endogenous BUB-1.
claims.source: Importantly, all of these mCherry-tagged mutants localised to kinetochores in absence of endogenous BUB-1, allowing us to test their influence on kinetochore-microtubule attachments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: BUB-1ΔKD prevents HCP-1CENP-F kinetochore localization.
claims.source: Interestingly, BUB-1ΔKD prevented HCP-1CENP-F kinetochore localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: BUB1 recruitment of CENP-F via its kinase domain is conserved from humans to C. elegans.
claims.source: suggesting that BUB1 recruitment of CENP-F via its kinase domain is conserved from humans to C. elegans (Ciossani et al., 2018; Raaijmakers et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claims.claim: The presence of mainly bioriented chromosomes with amphitelic attachments in BUB-1ΔKD mutant suggests that BUB-1's inhibitory role during biorientation is dependent on the kinase domain.
claims.source: Furthermore, the presence of mainly bioriented chromosomes with amphitelic attachments in this mutant that lacks kinetochore HCP-1/2CENP-F, suggests that BUB-1's inhibitory role during biorientation is dependent on the kinase domain.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N attenuate the HCP-1/2CENP-F loss-of-function phenotype, allowing delayed but successful chromosome congression and biorientation with merotelic attachments.
claims.source: In contrast, the phenotype was attenuated with BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R ;D847N: chromosome congression was delayed but occurred successfully (Figure 3B,C; Video 3), and chromosome biorientation with merotelic attachments was established (Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3B-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The appearance of merotelic attachments only after depletion of HCP-1/2CENP-F in BUB-1ΔKD suggests that HCP-1/2CENP-F promote non-merotelic attachments independently of its kinetochore localization.
claims.source: The appearance of a large proportion of merotelic attachments only after depletion of HCP-1/2CENP-F in BUB-1ΔKD (which normally lacks kinetochore-associated HCP-1/2CENP-F) suggests that HCP-1/2CENP-F promote non-merotelic attachments independently of its kinetochore localization (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The integrity of the kinase domain is required for BUB-1 inhibition of chromosome congression and biorientation.
claims.source: Furthermore, these results confirm that the integrity of the kinase domain is required for BUB-1 inhibition of chromosome congression and biorientation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: The HCP-1/2CENP-F loss-of-function phenotype is not rescued by BUB-1D814N, which specifically disrupts the kinase activity.
claims.source: In contrast, the HCP-1/2CENP-F loss-of-function phenotype was not rescued by BUB-1D814N, which specifically disrupts the kinase activity (Figure 3B–D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E) (Moyle et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 3B-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: BUB-1's inhibitory role on biorientation depends on its kinase domain, but not its kinase activity.
claims.source: Altogether, these results demonstrate that BUB-1's inhibitory role on biorientation depends on its kinase domain, but not its kinase activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: In mammals, BUB1 contributes to recruiting the RZZ complex, and thus probably also dynein-dynactin, to kinetochores.
claims.source: In mammals, BUB1 contributes to recruiting the RZZ complex, and thus probably also dynein-dynactin, to kinetochores (Caldas et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claims.claim: BUB-1 depletion leads to a drastic reduction of ZWL-1Zwilch at kinetochores.
claims.source: Consistent with previous results in human cells, BUB-1 depletion led to a drastic reduction of the GFP-tagged RZZ complex component ZWL-1Zwilch at kinetochores (Figure 4B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: BUB-1 depletion leads to complete loss of DNC-2p50 from kinetochores.
claims.source: Reduction in RZZ kinetochore targeting coincided with the complete loss of the GFP-tagged dynactin subunit DNC-2p50 from kinetochores, which instead localized diffusely on chromosomes and in the spindle region (Figure 4B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: BUB-1 is required for dynein-dynactin recruitment to kinetochores in C. elegans zygotes.
claims.source: Therefore BUB-1 is required for dynein-dynactin recruitment to kinetochores in C. elegans zygotes, and the residual pool of RZZ complex that localises to kinetochores independently of BUB-1 does not contribute to dynein-dynactin recruitment.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: Both ZWL-1Zwilch and DNC-2p50 are present at kinetochores in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: Importantly, both ZWL-1Zwilch and DNC-2p50 were present at kinetochores in absence of HCP-1/2 CENP-F (Figure 4B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-D.

claims.claim: Co-depletion of ZWL-1Zwilch with HCP-1CENP-F leads to slight improvement in chromosome congression, and chromosome segregation occurs later and more slowly than in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F alone.
claims.source: For this, we co-depleted ZWL-1Zwilch with HCP-1CENP-F in the Δhcp-2 strain. This led to a slight improvement in chromosome congression, and chromosome segregation occurred later and more slowly than in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F alone (Figure 4C,D; Video 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4C,D and Video 4.

claims.claim: RZZ and dynein promote rapid end-on attachments and early co-segregation of sister chromatids in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: This result suggests that RZZ and dynein promote rapid end-on attachments and early co-segregation of sister chromatids in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: Chromosome biorientation is not restored and sister chromatids still co-segregate upon co-depletion of ZWL-1Zwilch and HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: However, chromosome biorientation was not restored and sister chromatid still co-segregated in this condition (Figure 4C–E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1E; Video 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: BUB-1ΔKD mutant supports normal recruitment of DNC-2p50 but does not inhibit chromosome biorientation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: Further evidence confirming the independence of BUB-1 activities in inhibiting chromosome biorientation and in recruiting RZZ and dynein-dynactin came from our analysis of the BUB-1ΔKD mutant, which could support the normal recruitment of DNC-2p50 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F) but did not inhibit chromosome biorientation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F (Figure 3B–D).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and Figure 3B-D.

claims.claim: Kinetochore recruitment of RZZ and dynein-dynactin by BUB-1 is important for initial end-on attachments, but does not explain BUB-1 inhibition of chromosome biorientation.
claims.source: Therefore, kinetochore recruitment of RZZ and dynein-dynactin by BUB-1 is important for initial end-on attachments, but does not explain BUB-1 inhibition of chromosome biorientation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1ΔKD mutant leads to a decreased frequency of merotelic attachments and reduced kinetochore stretches in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: However, in contrast to the full BUB-1 depletion, the BUB-1ΔKD mutant also led to a decreased frequency of merotelic attachments (Figures 3D and 4E) and reduced kinetochore stretches in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figures 3D, 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: The high degree of merotely observed upon BUB-1 codepletion with HCP-1/2CENP-F is largely caused by the loss of dynein from kinetochores.
claims.source: This suggests that the high degree of merotely observed upon BUB-1 codepletion with HCP-1/2CENP-F is largely caused by the loss of dynein from kinetochores, and that BUB-1 favours amphitelic attachments by recruiting dynein to kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 favours amphitelic attachments by recruiting dynein to kinetochores.
claims.source: This suggests that the high degree of merotely observed upon BUB-1 codepletion with HCP-1/2CENP-F is largely caused by the loss of dynein from kinetochores, and that BUB-1 favours amphitelic attachments by recruiting dynein to kinetochores.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: Recruiting the RZZ complex and dynein-dynactin at the kinetochore is a critical function of BUB-1 to promote amphitelic end-on attachments.
claims.source: Altogether, these results suggest that recruiting the RZZ complex and dynein-dynactin at the kinetochore is a critical function of BUB-1 to promote amphitelic end-on attachments (Gassmann et al., 2008a).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 inhibits chromosome congression and biorientation independently of AIR-2Aurora B activity.
claims.source: Upon upshift of HCP-1/2CENP-F-depleted air-2(ts) mutant embryos to the restrictive temperature, sister chromatids still co-segregated prematurely (100 s after NEBD). Therefore BUB-1 inhibits chromosome congression and biorientation independently of AIR-2Aurora B activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C.

claims.claim: GFP-tagged SKA-1 is undetectable at kinetochores in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: Accordingly, we found that GFP-tagged SKA-1 was undetectable at kinetochores in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B.

claims.claim: SKA-1 kinetochore localization depends on the tension exerted at kinetochores by end-on attachments.
claims.source: However, as SKA-1 kinetochore localization depends on the tension exerted at kinetochores by end-on attachments (Cheerambathur et al., 2017)
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claims.claim: Mono-oriented attachments in ZYG-1Plk4-depleted 2 cell stage embryos provide sufficient tension for SKA complex kinetochore localization.
claims.source: In this condition, SKA-1::GFP accumulated on the chromosome side that faces the spindle monopole, demonstrating that mono-oriented attachments in ZYG-1Plk4-depleted 2 cell stage embryos provide sufficient tension for SKA complex kinetochore localization (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,C).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,C.

claims.claim: SKA-1 kinetochore recruitment is inhibited in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F, but the mono-oriented attachment configuration is not sufficient to account for the lack of kinetochore SKA-1.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that SKA-1 kinetochore recruitment is inhibited in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F, but that the mono-oriented attachment configuration is not sufficient to account for the lack of kinetochore SKA-1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: SKA-1::GFP kinetochore recruitment is rescued by depleting BUB-1 in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: Most importantly, SKA-1::GFP kinetochore recruitment was rescued by depleting BUB-1 in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F (Figure 5B; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B)
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B.

claims.claim: BUB-1 prevents SKA-1 recruitment to kinetochores when HCP-1/2CENP-F is absent.
claims.source: suggesting that BUB-1 prevents SKA-1 recruitment to kinetochores when HCP-1/2CENP-F is absent.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: Both BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N mutants allow kinetochore recruitment of SKA-1::GFP.
claims.source: In agreement with our first prediction, both mutants allowed kinetochore recruitment of SKA-1::GFP (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2F.

claims.claim: In the simultaneous absence of endogenous BUB-1, HCP-1/2CENP-F and SKA-1, both BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N mutants lead to complete failure of chromosome congression and biorientation.
claims.source: Strikingly in the simultaneous absence of endogenous BUB-1, HCP-1/2CENP-F and SKA-1, both BUB-1 mutants (BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R ;D847N) led to complete failure of chromosome congression and biorientation, along with sister chromatid co-segregation, similar to what is observed after HCP-1/2CENP-F depletion alone (Figure 5C–E; Figure 5—figure supplement 2G; Video 5).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 5C-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2G.

claims.claim: BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N are capable of sustaining chromosome biorientation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F only when the SKA complex is present.
claims.source: Thus BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R ;D847N are capable of sustaining chromosome biorientation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F only when the SKA complex is present.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: In BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N mutants, the kinetochore-localized SKA complex is responsible for the observed rescue of chromosome biorientation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.source: This result suggests that in these two BUB-1 mutants the kinetochore-localized SKA complex is responsible for the observed rescue of chromosome biorientation in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: In absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP, BUB-1 inhibits stable biorientation of chromosomes by preventing SKA complex recruitment to kinetochores.
claims.source: Altogether, our results suggest that, in absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP, BUB-1 inhibits stable biorientation of chromosomes by preventing SKA complex recruitment to kinetochores (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: The phenotype of premature sister chromatid co-segregation upon loss of CLS-2CLASP can be rescued by alleviating BUB-1-mediated inhibition of SKA-1 at the kinetochores.
claims.source: We found that this phenotype can be rescued by alleviating BUB-1-mediated inhibition of SKA-1 at the kinetochores, preventing SKA-mediated attachment maturation.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and is based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: The capacity for chromosomes to engage in stable connections to both spindle poles can be provided either by efficient kinetochore microtubule polymerization or by kinetochore-microtubule attachment maturation.
claims.source: These observations suggest that the capacity for chromosomes to engage in stable connections to both spindle poles can be provided either by efficient kinetochore microtubule polymerization or by kinetochore-microtubule attachment maturation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 provides two opposing activities in the establishment of bioriented amphitelic connections: promoting biorientation by recruiting CLS-2CLASP to kinetochores, and restricting biorientation by limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation.
claims.source: Thus, BUB-1 provides two opposing activities in the establishment of bioriented amphitelic connections: (1) promoting biorientation by recruiting CLS-2CLASP to kinetochores, and (2) restricting biorientation by limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: Embryos expressing BUB-1ΔKD only present slight merotely at 24°C, but lowering the temperature to 15°C raises the rate of merotely by three-fold.
claims.source: Embryos expressing BUB-1ΔKD only presented slight merotely at 24°C, but lowering the temperature down to 15°C, and therefore lowering overall microtubule growth (Srayko et al., 2005), raised this rate of merotely by three-fold (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: A similar temperature dependency for embryonic lethality is observed in the BUB-1ΔKD mutant.
claims.source: We observed a similar temperature dependency for embryonic lethality in this mutant (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Promoting kinetochore microtubule assembly via BUB-1-mediated recruitment of CLS-2CLASP is required to avoid merotely and embryonic lethality.
claims.source: These results suggest that promoting kinetochore microtubule assembly via BUB-1-mediated recruitment of CLS-2CLASP is required to avoid merotely and embryonic lethality.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1K718R;D847N mutant-expressing embryos display up to 21% embryonic lethality when raised at 24°C.
claims.source: In contrast to control BUB-1WT-expressing embryos, we found that BUB-1K718R ;D847N mutant-expressing embryos displayed up to 21% embryonic lethality when raised at 24°C.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Embryos depleted of MDF-1Mad1 do not show the same temperature-dependent lethality as BUB-1K718R;D847N mutant embryos.
claims.source: Embryos depleted of the SAC protein MDF-1Mad1 did not show the same temperature-dependent lethality (8%), nor did the BUB-1D814N mutant (3.4%).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The BUB-1K718R;D847N mutant phenotype is not caused by a defective SAC or a lack of BUB-1 kinase activity, but rather by the enhanced microtubule growth at high temperature.
claims.source: The BUB-1K718R ;D847N mutant phenotype is therefore not caused by a defective SAC or a lack of BUB-1 kinase activity, but rather by the enhanced microtubule growth at high temperature (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: When load-bearing connections are favoured by high microtubule dynamics, limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation becomes essential.
claims.source: In other words, when load-bearing connections are favoured by high microtubule dynamics, limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation becomes essential.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 displays opposing activities at the kinetochore to promote properly bioriented kinetochore-microtubule attachments and to prevent embryonic lethality.
claims.source: Together, our data suggest that BUB-1 displays opposing activities at the kinetochore to promote properly bioriented kinetochore-microtubule attachments and to prevent embryonic lethality.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on the experimental data presented.

claims.claim: BUB-1 has two previously uncharacterized functions: accelerating end-on kinetochore-microtubule attachments by recruiting the dynein-dynactin complex to kinetochores, and limiting attachment maturation by the SKA complex.
claims.source: Here, we identify two previously uncharacterized functions of the C. elegans BUB-1 kinase in (1) accelerating end-on kinetochore-microtubule attachments by recruiting the dynein-dynactin complex to kinetochores, and (2) limiting attachment maturation by the SKA complex (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is a summary of the primary findings.

claims.claim: BUB-1's activity in limiting attachment maturation by the SKA complex relies on the BUB-1 kinase domain but is independent of kinase activity.

results.result: BUB-1 is a conserved SAC protein that also has non-SAC roles in chromosome segregation across multiple species including yeast, C. elegans, and human cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C12-C15 establish the dual role of BUB-1 as both a SAC component and a regulator of chromosome segregation independently of the SAC. These claims are well-supported by citations to prior work and provide the foundational context for the study.

results.result: BUB-1 depletion delays load-bearing kinetochore-microtubule attachments and leads to merotelic attachments, as evidenced by delayed chromosome congression, a spindle pole 'bump', and bent kinetochores during metaphase.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C29 describe the phenotype of BUB-1 depletion with supporting data from Figure 1B,C and Video 1. The observations of delayed congression, the pole separation bump, and merotelic attachments are consistent and well-documented with imaging data.

results.result: BUB-1 recruits HCP-1/2CENP-F and CLS-2CLASP to kinetochores; depletion of HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP results in mono-oriented chromosomes and premature sister chromatid co-segregation without premature anaphase onset.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C36 establish the epistatic relationship between BUB-1, HCP-1/2CENP-F, and CLS-2CLASP. The data in Figure 1B-H and Video 1, along with the separase sensor experiments (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-E), provide strong evidence for these conclusions.

results.result: Co-depletion of BUB-1 with HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP rescues chromosome biorientation, revealing that BUB-1 prevents chromosome biorientation in the absence of these proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C40 describe a key genetic interaction showing that BUB-1 inhibits biorientation when HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP are absent. This is supported by data in Figure 1B,C and Video 1, demonstrating rescue of the segregation defect.

results.result: BUB-1's inhibitory activity on chromosome biorientation requires its kinetochore localization, as demonstrated using a KNL-1Δ85-505 mutant that lacks MELT repeats and abolishes BUB-1 kinetochore recruitment.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C44 demonstrate that BUB-1 must be at the kinetochore to exert its inhibitory effect. The use of the KNL-1Δ85-505 mutant (Figure 2) provides a clean genetic test of this requirement, and the results are consistent with the hypothesis.

results.result: BUB-1's inhibitory role in chromosome biorientation depends on its kinase domain but not its kinase activity, as shown by analysis of BUB-1ΔKD, BUB-1K718R;D847N, and BUB-1D814N mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C54 systematically dissect BUB-1 function using three different mutants. The data in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 show that the kinase domain is required but kinase activity is not, providing strong mechanistic insight.

results.result: BUB-1 is required for kinetochore recruitment of the RZZ complex and dynein-dynactin in C. elegans, as shown by loss of ZWL-1Zwilch and complete loss of DNC-2p50 from kinetochores upon BUB-1 depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C59 establish BUB-1's role in recruiting RZZ and dynein-dynactin. The data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-D show clear reduction in ZWL-1 and complete loss of DNC-2 from kinetochores upon BUB-1 depletion.

results.result: RZZ and dynein-dynactin promote rapid end-on attachments but their recruitment by BUB-1 does not explain BUB-1's inhibition of chromosome biorientation, as co-depletion of ZWL-1 with HCP-1/2CENP-F does not restore biorientation.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C64 demonstrate that RZZ/dynein recruitment is separable from BUB-1's inhibitory activity. The data in Figure 4C-E and Video 4, along with analysis of the BUB-1ΔKD mutant, support this conclusion.

results.result: BUB-1 recruitment of dynein-dynactin to kinetochores is critical for preventing merotelic attachments and promoting amphitelic end-on attachments, as evidenced by reduced merotely in the BUB-1ΔKD mutant compared to full BUB-1 depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C68 establish the importance of BUB-1-mediated dynein recruitment for preventing merotely. The comparison between BUB-1 depletion and BUB-1ΔKD (Figures 3D, 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1G) provides clear evidence for this function.

results.result: BUB-1 inhibits chromosome congression and biorientation independently of AIR-2Aurora B activity, as shown using a temperature-sensitive AIR-2 mutant.
results.evaluation: Claim C69 rules out Aurora B as a mediator of BUB-1's inhibitory activity. The use of the air-2(ts) mutant (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C) provides a direct test of this hypothesis, and the results are clear.

results.result: BUB-1 prevents SKA-1 recruitment to kinetochores in the absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F, as demonstrated by the absence of SKA-1 at kinetochores in HCP-1/2CENP-F-depleted embryos and its rescue upon BUB-1 co-depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C75 establish BUB-1's role in inhibiting SKA complex recruitment. The data in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B, including the monopolar spindle control experiment, provide strong evidence for this mechanism.

results.result: BUB-1 mutants (BUB-1ΔKD and BUB-1K718R;D847N) that allow SKA complex recruitment can sustain chromosome biorientation in the absence of HCP-1/2CENP-F only when the SKA complex is present, demonstrating that BUB-1 inhibits biorientation by preventing SKA complex recruitment.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C80 provide the key mechanistic test of BUB-1's inhibitory activity. The data in Figure 5C-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2F,G show that SKA-1 deletion abolishes the rescue phenotype of BUB-1 mutants, strongly supporting the proposed mechanism.

results.result: BUB-1 provides two opposing activities in establishing bioriented amphitelic connections: promoting biorientation by recruiting CLS-2CLASP and restricting biorientation by limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C83 synthesize the findings into a coherent model of BUB-1's dual activities. This conclusion is well-supported by the cumulative evidence from the genetic rescue experiments and mutant analyses.

results.result: Promoting kinetochore microtubule assembly via BUB-1-mediated recruitment of CLS-2CLASP is required to avoid merotely and embryonic lethality, as shown by temperature-dependent increases in merotely and lethality in BUB-1ΔKD embryos.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C86 demonstrate the physiological importance of BUB-1's role in recruiting CLS-2CLASP. The temperature-dependent phenotype (Figure 6A,B) provides strong evidence linking microtubule dynamics to merotely and viability.

results.result: Limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation by BUB-1 is essential when microtubule dynamics are high, as demonstrated by temperature-dependent embryonic lethality in BUB-1K718R;D847N mutants that is not observed in SAC-deficient or kinase-dead mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C91 demonstrate the importance of BUB-1's inhibitory activity on SKA. The temperature-dependent lethality of BUB-1K718R;D847N (Figure 6C) and the controls ruling out SAC and kinase activity defects provide strong support.

results.result: BUB-1 has a central role in promoting accurate chromosome biorientation by coordinating multiple activities: accelerating end-on attachments via dynein-dynactin recruitment, promoting amphitelic attachments via CLS-2CLASP, and limiting attachment maturation by the SKA complex.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C98 summarize the main findings of the study. These conclusions are well-supported by the cumulative experimental evidence presented throughout the manuscript.

results.result: BUB-1 contributes to RZZ kinetochore recruitment in C. elegans, but does not fully abrogate it, consistent with the existence of alternative RZZ recruitment pathways independent of BUB1 and Zwint observed in human cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C105 place the findings in the context of prior work in human cells. The observation of residual RZZ at kinetochores after BUB-1 depletion (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B) is consistent with the literature on alternative recruitment pathways.

results.result: BUB-1 both recruits dynein-dynactin via the RZZ complex and stabilizes it at kinetochores via HCP-1/2CENP-F and NUD-2NudE/el, with both activities contributing to rapid and accurate establishment of biorientation.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C110 propose a model for how BUB-1 ensures complete dynein-dynactin recruitment. The functional analysis comparing BUB-1 depletion with BUB-1ΔKD (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G) supports this dual mechanism.

results.result: BUB-1 antagonizes CLS-2CLASP-dependent kinetochore microtubule assembly by limiting SKA complex-mediated attachment maturation, as chromosomes become bioriented upon HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP depletion only when BUB-1 is absent.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C114 integrate the findings on BUB-1's dual roles. This conclusion is well-supported by the genetic rescue experiments and provides a coherent explanation for the observed phenotypes.

results.result: The mechanism by which BUB-1 limits SKA complex recruitment remains unclear, with potential mechanisms including direct inhibition, indirect regulation via Aurora A-mediated NDC80 phosphorylation, or modulation of kinetochore tension.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C121 discuss possible mechanisms but are largely speculative. While the monopolar spindle experiment (C119) provides some data, the other possibilities (C115, C117, C120, C121) are not directly tested and remain hypothetical.

results.result: BUB-1 is hyper-recruited to kinetochores upon HCP-1/2CENP-F depletion, suggesting that a threshold level of BUB-1 may be required to prevent SKA complex localization, and that depleting HCP-1/2CENP-F or CLS-2CLASP amplifies BUB-1's inhibitory activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C125 describe an interesting observation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2H,I) but the interpretation is speculative. The threshold model (C124) and amplification hypothesis (C125) are plausible but not directly tested.

results.result: BUB-1 functions as a temporal regulator of kinetochore-microtubule attachments, coordinating initial end-on attachments, attachment stability, and maturation, with its progressive departure from kinetochores in metaphase allowing SKA complex accumulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C132 present a temporal model of BUB-1 function. The model is supported by the kinetics data (Figure 6D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2H,I) and the embryonic lethality data demonstrating the importance of coordinating these activities.

results.result: BUB-1's non-SAC role in limiting SKA-mediated attachment maturation, which depends on the kinase domain but not kinase activity, may be a conserved function of BUB1 in metazoans, as suggested by similar requirements in human HAP1 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C136 place the findings in a broader evolutionary context. The parallel between C. elegans BUB-1 and human BUB1 in HAP1 cells (C135) supports the conservation hypothesis, though direct functional conservation remains to be tested.

results.result: The NDC80 complex and RZZ-Spindly module are the two main kinetochore microtubule-binding modules in metazoans, with NDC80 establishing load-bearing end-coupled connections, RZZ/dynein mediating initial lateral capture and orientation, and the SKA complex reinforcing load-bearing connections.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C11 provide background knowledge on kinetochore-microtubule attachment mechanisms. These are well-established facts from the literature, supported by multiple citations, and provide essential context for the study.

results.result: BUB1 mediates recruitment of several downstream proteins including Aurora B/PP2A via H2A phosphorylation and Shugoshin, CENP-F via its kinase domain, and the RZZ complex, but the mechanism of its non-SAC role in chromosome segregation remains unclear.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C21 summarize prior knowledge about BUB1's downstream effectors and establish the gap in understanding that the study addresses. These claims are well-supported by citations and provide important context.

results.result: In C. elegans zygotes, holocentric kinetochores form along the length of sister chromatids, spindle pole separation is driven by cortical pulling forces, and pole-to-pole distance serves as an indirect readout of load-bearing kinetochore-microtubule connections.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C140 describe the C. elegans system and the experimental approach. These are well-established facts supported by citations and provide essential methodological context for interpreting the results.
